elements.element: Audits may occur no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Section 22.1 states: “No more than once in any twelve-month period.”

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' prior written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Section 22.1 requires “at least thirty days' prior written notice.”

elements.element: Audits must occur during Customer's business hours.
elements.evidence: Section 22.1 limits audits to “Customer's normal business hours.”

elements.element: Each audit must be conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: Section 22.1 states that the audit shall be conducted by an independent auditor.

elements.element: The independent auditor must be bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: Section 22.1 requires written confidentiality obligations at least as protective as Section 16.

elements.element: Vendor must bear audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding 5%.
elements.evidence: Section 22.2 makes Vendor bear audit costs unless underpayment exceeds five percent for the audited period.

elements.element: Vendor and its auditor must have no direct access to Customer systems.
elements.evidence: Section 22.1 provides that Vendor and its auditor shall have no access to Customer's systems, and Section 22.2 separately prohibits direct system access.

elements.element: Audits may occur no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The rolling limitation of once in any twelve-month period is at least as restrictive as once per year.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: The operative clause requires at least thirty days' prior written notice, which exceeds the 15-day requirement.

elements.element: Vendor must bear audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding 10%.
elements.evidence: Section 22.2 shifts reasonable audit costs to Customer when underpayment exceeds five percent, including underpayments above 5% but not exceeding 10%.

result.reason: The operative redline satisfies every preferred requirement. It independently fails the fallback cost-allocation threshold because costs can shift at an underpayment exceeding 5%, rather than only when underpayment exceeds 10%. The edits are confined to implementing the audit safeguards and leave the existing confidentiality, reporting, payment, and finality provisions effective. Drafting is clear, though the system-access prohibition is duplicative across Sections 22.1 and 22.2.
